findings.title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the 5-arg version
findings.body: Ruby has no overloading, so the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers that pass width and height separately will now treat max_height as `opts` (an Integer), and `opts[:allow_animation]` or `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` will raise or be ignored. Dimensions will also be wrong. The first definition is dead code. Keep one signature and update the callers.

findings.title: Downsize loop can corrupt or ignore failures, and mishandles animated GIFs
findings.body: The return value of `downsize` is ignored, so if convert fails the loop repeats 5 times for nothing. The in-place conversion (from == to) on a tempfile can also lose the original. After downsizing, `tempfile.size` may be stale, because `File#size` on a Tempfile can be cached or buffered. The upload then uses the old size. For GIFs the gifsicle path uses `--resize-fit` with "80%", which is not a valid dimension argument, so it fails. If the image is still too big after the loop, the upload goes ahead and is later rejected with a confusing error.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores the site settings
findings.body: The client-side limit is now hardcoded to 10MB, so the `max_attachment_size_kb` setting is no longer enforced on the client. Admins who set a lower limit get no client-side validation. The 413 error message likewise shows 10MB instead of the real limit. The server-side download limit in the controller is also hardcoded to 10MB.
